# 1 Kings Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-it-was in-the-four-hundred and-eightieth year after-the-going-out-of the-sons-of Israel from-the-land-of Egypt, in-the-fourth year, in-the-month-of Ziv — it is the-second month — of-the-reigning-of Solomon over Israel, and-he-built the-house for-YHWH.

**2** And-the-house that the-king Solomon built for-YHWH — sixty cubits its-length, and-twenty its-width, and-thirty cubits its-height.

**3** And-the-porch before the-temple-of the-house — twenty cubits its-length, upon the-face-of the-width-of the-house; ten cubits its-depth upon the-face-of the-house.

**4** And-he-made for-the-house windows-of narrowing frames.

**5** And-he-built against the-wall-of the-house a-structure all-around — against-the-walls-of the-house all-around, for-the-temple and-for-the-inner-sanctuary — and-he-made side-chambers all-around.

**6** The-lowest story — five cubits its-width, and-the-middle — six cubits its-width, and-the-third — seven cubits its-width. For he-made offsets in-the-wall-of the-house all-around on-the-outside, so-as-not to-fasten in-the-walls-of the-house.

**7** And-the-house, in-its-being-built, of-whole stone from-the-quarry was-built; and-hammer and-axe — any tool-of iron — was-not heard in-the-house in-its-being-built.

**8** The-entrance-of the-lowest side-chamber was in-the-right shoulder-of the-house, and-by-winding-stairs they-would-go-up to the-middle, and-from the-middle to the-third.

**9** And-he-built ʾet-the-house, and-finished-it. And-he-covered ʾet-the-house with-beams and-rows-of cedar.

**10** And-he-built ʾet-the-structure against all the-house — five cubits its-height — and-it-held the-house with-timber-of cedar.

**11** And-the-word-of YHWH came to Solomon, saying,

**12** "This house that you are-building — if you-walk in-my-statutes and-ʾet-my-judgments you-do, and-keep ʾet-all my-commandments to-walk in-them, then-I-will-establish ʾet-my-word with-you that I-spoke to David your-father.

**13** And-I-will-dwell in-the-midst-of the-sons-of Israel, and-I-will-not forsake ʾet-my-people Israel."

**14** And-Solomon built ʾet-the-house and-finished-it.

**15** And-he-built ʾet-the-walls-of the-house on-the-inside with-boards-of cedar — from the-floor-of the-house to the-walls-of the-ceiling he-overlaid with-wood on-the-inside — and-he-overlaid ʾet-the-floor-of the-house with-boards-of cypress.

**16** And-he-built ʾet-the-twenty cubits from-the-rear-of the-house with-boards-of cedar from the-floor to the-walls, and-he-built for-it on-the-inside the-inner-sanctuary, the-Holy-of-Holies.

**17** And-forty cubits was the-house — it is the-temple — before-it.

**18** And-cedar on-the-house on-the-inside — carvings-of gourds and-open flowers — all was cedar; no stone was-seen.

**19** And-the-inner-sanctuary in-the-midst-of the-house on-the-inside he-prepared, to-set there ʾet-the-ark-of the-covenant-of YHWH.

**20** And-the-face-of the-inner-sanctuary — twenty cubits in-length, and-twenty cubits in-width, and-twenty cubits its-height. And-he-overlaid-it with-gold refined. And-he-overlaid the-altar with-cedar.

**21** And-Solomon overlaid ʾet-the-house on-the-inside with-gold refined, and-he-drew chains-of gold before the-inner-sanctuary, and-he-overlaid-it with-gold.

**22** And-ʾet-all the-house he-overlaid with-gold until all the-house was-finished. And-all the-altar that was-by the-inner-sanctuary he-overlaid with-gold.

**23** And-he-made in-the-inner-sanctuary two cherubim of-olive wood — ten cubits their-height.

**24** And-five cubits was-the-one wing-of the-cherub, and-five cubits the-second wing-of the-cherub — ten cubits from-the-tip-of his-wing to the-tip-of his-wing.

**25** And-ten cubits was the-second cherub — one measure and-one form for-the-two cherubim.

**26** The-height-of the-one cherub was ten cubits, and-so the-second cherub.

**27** And-he-set ʾet-the-cherubim in-the-midst-of the-inner house. And-they-spread ʾet-the-wings-of the-cherubim, and-the-wing-of the-one touched the-wall, and-the-wing-of the-second cherub touched the-second wall. And-their-wings toward-the-middle-of the-house were-touching wing to wing.

**28** And-he-overlaid ʾet-the-cherubim with-gold.

**29** And-ʾet-all the-walls-of the-house all-around he-carved with-carvings-of cherubim and-palm-trees and-open flowers — on-the-inside and-on-the-outside.

**30** And-ʾet-the-floor-of the-house he-overlaid with-gold — on-the-inside and-on-the-outside.

**31** And-ʾet-the-entrance-of the-inner-sanctuary he-made doors-of olive wood; the-pillar and-the-doorposts were a-fifth.

**32** And-the-two doors were-of olive wood, and-he-carved upon-them carvings-of cherubim and-palm-trees and-open flowers, and-overlaid with-gold. And-he-spread ʾet-the-gold upon the-cherubim and-upon the-palm-trees.

**33** And-so he-made for-the-entrance-of the-temple doorposts-of olive wood — from a-fourth.

**34** And-two doors of-cypress wood — the-two leaves-of the-one door were-folding, and-the-two leaves-of the-second door were-folding.

**35** And-he-carved cherubim and-palm-trees and-open flowers, and-overlaid with-gold fitted upon the-carved-work.

**36** And-he-built ʾet-the-inner court — three rows-of hewn stone and-a-row-of cedar beams.

**37** In-the-fourth year was-laid the-foundation-of the-house-of YHWH, in-the-month-of Ziv.

**38** And-in-the-eleventh year, in-the-month-of Bul — it is the-eighth month — the-house was-finished in-all its-matters and-in-all its-specifications. And-he-built-it in-seven years.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **6:1 — "four-hundred and-eightieth year"**: This chronological anchor connects the temple to the Exodus — the foundational act of Israel's history. The temple is the architectural culmination of deliverance.

2. **6:7 — "no hammer... was heard"**: Stones were pre-cut at the quarry so that no iron tool sounded at the construction site. This detail elevates the building process itself to an act of reverence — the silence of sacred construction.

3. **6:12-13 — the conditional word**: God interrupts the building narrative with a condition: the temple's validity depends on obedience, not architecture. The house of stone is secondary to the house of faithfulness.

4. **6:20 — "twenty cubits... twenty cubits... twenty cubits"**: The inner sanctuary is a perfect cube — the same proportional geometry as the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle, now at monumental scale. The cube symbolizes completeness and perfection.

5. **6:29 — cherubim, palm-trees, open flowers**: This decorative program evokes Eden — the garden paradise that was lost. The temple's interior recreates the primeval sacred space where God and humanity once dwelt together.

— EMET
